originalTitle: Nasdaq suffers worst month in over a year as AI nerves roil markets
summary: Wall Street suffered a steep day of losses Friday after the latest tech earnings reignited concerns that massive spending on AI may not deliver the returns that investors expect.
content: Wall Street suffered a steep day of losses Friday after the latest tech earnings reignited concerns that massive spending on AI may not deliver the returns that investors expect. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.86% and the S&P 500 fell 1.82%, each suffering their worst day since June. The Dow fell 572 points, or roughly 1.1%. Just a few weeks ago, the Nasdaq and S&P 500 clinched record highs. But markets were rattled this month as concerns festered about higher interest rates, tech companies burning through cash on enormous AI spending and weaker-than-expected earnings and forecasts. The Nasdaq is now down 7.8% from its record high earlier this month and suffered its worst monthly decline since March 2025. The S&P 500 is down roughly 3% since its peak. Intel plunged 28.58% Friday, its worst day since 1974 and second-worst day on record, after issuing weaker guidance for the fourth quarter, citing weakness in the PC market because higher memory chip costs are hurting consumer demand. Amazon shares also dropped, falling 1.4%, following an earnings report that indicated further increases in AI spending while the company’s sales and profit results missed analysts’ expectations. This comes after shares of Alphabet — Google’s parent company — sank by more than 12% Thursday, wiping half a trillion dollars off the market value of America’s fourth-largest company. Investors were concerned about a slowdown in Google’s search advertising business and a ramp-up in AI spending. Alphabet shares fell another 1.4% on Friday, capping off their worst month on record. Investors’ concerns about the AI boom rattled other semiconductor chipmakers: Nvidia shares dropped 4.2%, while a closely watched index of chipmakers sank 7.2%. Big Tech spending under the spotlight Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon are collectively spending hundreds of billions of dollars on building data centers. After cheering on anything AI-related, Wall Street is getting more discerning about which companies are spending rationally and seeing tangible returns on investment. Friday was the final trading day of a bruising month for AI stocks as investors continue to scrutinize the enormous cost of the AI boom and demand evidence that those investments will eventually translate into profit. “We’re moving out of the hopes and dreams phase of the AI trade and into the ‘show me’ phase,” Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, said in a note. “Full order books are great, but investors want to see who can actually deliver, turn that demand into earnings and generate cash,” he said. Alphabet’s earnings results on Wednesday ignited concerns that Google’s core business of search advertising revenue is threatened by consumers using AI chatbots instead of traditional search. Alphabet’s promise of returns from AI “is getting pushed even further down the road,” Matt Maley, chief strategist at Miller Tabak + Co, said in a note. “It raises the question as to whether the payout will be as big as they have been promising.” As Big Tech ramps up its spending, investors are getting nervous about its impact to their balance sheets. Alphabet just posted two quarters of negative free cash flow for the first time on record as AI spending accelerates while revenue isn’t growing as fast as expected. Meta last week disclosed a quarter of negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012. Amazon on Thursday announced it had negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the past 12 months as the company ramps up AI spending. “Investors don’t just want capex, they want to see the returns already,” Neil Wilson, a strategist at Saxo Markets, said in a note. “For the wider AI trade, we are starting to see a more critical evaluation of the return on investment from this monster AI splurge.” Alphabet and Meta are in a bear market, down more than 20% since their peaks in May and August 2025, respectively. In contrast to Alphabet, Meta and Amazon, Microsoft this week announced $18.6 billion in positive free cash flow this past quarter, and its stock is down just 4% since its record high earlier this month. Investors are increasingly pointing to companies’ race to secure capital — by tapping debt and equity markets — as a sign that the AI boom is entering a new phase. Higher interest rates are also weighing on riskier, debt-fueled corners of the AI buildout, adding to jitters. Rough October Anthropic’s highly anticipated filing for its initial public offering on Monday gave a brief boost to tech stocks, before the sentiment turned sour midweek over Big Tech earnings. “The AI trade is down, but not out,” said Paul Stanley, managing director at Arca, in a note Friday morning. “This is not the first tech and AI correction, and it won’t be the last. We are still in the very early stages of AI development, and pullbacks are par for the course.” Adding to market jitters Friday: Bitcoin fell more than 4% over the past day, hitting its lowest level in more than a month, after the world’s largest crypto exchange was hit by the biggest heist on record. After an enormous rally this year, investors’ expectations for chipmakers continue to rise, and companies are struggling to impress Wall Street. Despite losing nearly a third of its value on Friday, Intel shares are still up 78% this year. “A lot of these names, Intel is no exception, they just had a phenomenal year already. So, there’s definitely some profit taking as a result,” said Mike Dickson, head of research and quantitative strategies at Horizon Investments. As investors dumped tech stocks, they rotated into defensive parts of the market, like the consumer staples sector and government bonds. Other corners of the tech industry have also been rattled as investors scrutinize earnings and demand evidence that companies will benefit, rather than be threatened, by developments in AI. chineseTitle: 由于 AI 扰乱市场，纳斯达克指数遭遇一年多来最糟糕的一个月
chineseSummary: 周五，在最新的科技财报再次引发人们对人工智能的大规模支出可能无法带来投资者预期回报的担忧后，华尔街遭受了惨重的损失。
chineseContent: 周五，在最新的科技财报再次引发人们对人工智能的大规模支出可能无法带来投资者预期回报的担忧后，华尔街遭受了惨重的损失。纳斯达克综合指数下跌 2.86%，标准普尔 500 指数下跌 1.82%，均遭遇 6 月份以来最糟糕的一天。道指下跌 572 点，跌幅约为 1.1%。就在几周前，纳斯达克指数和标准普尔 500 指数创下历史新高。但本月市场动荡不安，因为人们对利率上升、科技公司因巨额人工智能支出而烧钱以及盈利和预测低于预期的担忧加剧。纳斯达克指数目前较本月早些时候的历史高位下跌 7.8%，并遭遇 2025 年 3 月以来最严重的月度跌幅。标准普尔 500 指数较峰值下跌约 3%。英特尔周五暴跌 28.58%，这是自 1974 年以来最糟糕的一天，也是有记录以来第二糟糕的一天，此前英特尔发布了较弱的第四季度指引，理由是个人电脑市场疲软，因为存储芯片成本上涨损害了消费者需求。亚马逊股价也下跌，下跌 1.4%，此前一份财报显示人工智能支出进一步增加，而该公司的销售和利润结果低于分析师的预期。此前，谷歌母公司 Alphabet 的股价周四下跌超过 12%，这家美国第四大公司的市值蒸发了 5000 亿美元。投资者担心谷歌搜索广告业务的放缓和人工智能支出的增加。 Alphabet 股价周五又下跌 1.4%，结束了有记录以来最糟糕的一个月。投资者对人工智能热潮的担忧令其他半导体芯片制造商感到不安：英伟达股价下跌 4.2%，而备受关注的芯片制造商指数则下跌 7.2%。聚光灯下的大型科技支出 Alphabet、微软、Meta
